title: Lease-free atomic unpin: prefetch-safe aging for GPU KV cache
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Continuous batching and aggressive prefetching improve throughput but complicate eviction correctness on GPU-resident KV caches. Existing approaches (pure LRU, TTL, prefix-aware trimming) rely on leases or heavy coordination to prevent races between prefetch, use, and eviction. Leases add allocation overhead and introduce tail latency when lease renewal contends with hot prefixes. Goal: design a lease-free, atomic unpin and aging protocol that preserves correctness invariants (no use-after-evict, prefix coherence, bounded staleness) while enabling aggressive prefetch and compact eviction to free GPU memory.
proposal: Introduce an optimistic atomic-unpin protocol combined with a two-phase aging window and small per-shard shadow queues. Key ideas: 1) Each cached prefix entry has a 1-bit live flag and an 8-bit epoch counter (wrap-aware). Prefetch sets live=1 and increments epoch locally. 2) Eviction proceeds in two phases: a soft-age pass (mark candidates and move to shard-local shadow queue) and a hard-evict pass where entries in the shadow queue are atomically tested against current epoch and live flag before actual reclamation. 3) Access path clears live=1 and optionally increments epoch to indicate continued liveness. 4) When batching/routing pipelines carry pointer references into GPU KV memory, they use a lightweight fence: a generation token extracted from the epoch; if eviction occurs concurrently, hard-evict checks token mismatch to abort reclamation. 5) To bound memory overhead, shadow queues are capped and use prioritized trimming (by effective TTL and access frequency). This scheme avoids heavyweight lease leases/remote coordinator while providing atomic semantics for unpinning and eviction decisions.
design_notes: - The epoch counter size is a lever: 8 bits gives 256 wrap steps; wrap handling uses monotonic counters on hosts to avoid mis-reclaims across long pauses. - Shadow queues are per-GPU-shard to avoid cross-device coordination. - Soft-age pass is cheap and can be run opportunistically during idle batches. - Batching paths must propagate generation tokens in RPC headers for function-calling/tooling where GPU memory pointers may survive async work. - For prefix-aware eviction, we treat prefixes as first-class keys: a prefix group holds a group-epoch updated on any subkey prefetch to ensure cohort safety. - Fallback policy: when shadow queue is full, degrade to TTL-first trimming to preserve throughput.
acceptance_criteria: - No observed use-after-free in integration test harness with 1M synthetic prefetched prefixes and continuous batching at 2000 qps for 24h. - End-to-end throughput loss <2% vs baseline prefetch-enabled runtime with leases disabled. - Average token latency p95 within SLA (<200ms for small model workload) after enabling atomic unpin. - Memory reclaimed post hard-evict within expected thresholds and GPU OOMs eliminated in stress runs. - Automated property-based tests that assert: (a) prefix-coherence: if a prefix group hard-evicts a subkey, no active generation token with older epoch remains; (b) bounded staleness: no entry remains in cache beyond TTL+window in absence of accesses.
tests_and_harness: - Add an integration harness under infra/kv-tests that runs mixed workload: prefetch-heavy producer, consumer with delayed pointer dereference, and eviction pressure orchestrator. Link: https://github.com/redwood/kv-tests/pull/204. - Property tests (quickcheck-style) validating epoch wrapping and concurrent prefetch/evict races. - Microbench: measure atomic unpin path cost in cycles and latency tail when scaled to 64 concurrent batching threads. - Canary rollout to dedicated-qa cluster with 1 GPU shard, traffic shadowing of 10% production traffic and strict OOM alarm. - Data collection: per-route metrics for soft-age/hard-evict counts, shadow-queue pressure, aborted-reclaims, and generation-token-mismatches.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated dev build with unit tests. 2) Deploy to staging and run 24h stress harness. 3) Canary on dedicated-qa (10% traffic) for 72h. 4) Enable in Dedicated non-critical customers with monitoring and automatic rollback on OOM or >5% latency regression. 5) Broad rollout after 2 weeks of stability and sign-off from SRE and benchmarks team.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: epoch wrap and token reuse could lead to false-negative safety checks. Mitigation: conservative epoch size and host monotonic counters; escalate if wrap frequency observed. - Risk: shadow-queue starvation causing temporary memory pressure. Mitigation: bounded queue with backpressure signals to prefetch orchestrator and TTL-based emergency trimming. - Risk: added code path complexity increases maintenance. Mitigation: keep core checks in a small, well-tested runtime module with strong unit coverage and clear invariants in code comments.
open_questions:
- What is the optimal epoch bit width for long-running on-prem clusters with months between restarts? (8 vs 16 bits)
- Should we make shadow-queue size adaptive per workload or expose as tuning knob to Dedicated customers?
- Do we need explicit cross-GPU coordination for multi-GPU prefix cohorts or is group-epoch per-shard sufficient?
